newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Jan-May current account gap at $12.952 bln.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Jan-May current account gap at $12.952 bln.

text.p: Brazil posted a current account balance of payments deficit of $12.952 billion in the first five months of 1997, the Central Bank said.
The bank did not give the value of the current account gap as a percentage of the gross domestic product.
In the January-to-May period last year, Brazil's current account gap was $6.052 billion.
The bank also said in a statement net foreign reserves at the end of May rose to $58.459 billion, compared with $55.288 billion in April.
According to the international liquidity concept which includes accounts receivable, foreign reserves were $59.279 billion in May, up from $56.171 billion in April.
In the last 12 months, Brazil's current account deficit reached $31.247 billion or 4.06 percent of GDP, the Central Bank said.

The bank also released consolidated current account deficit figures for the first quarter. Brazil posted a current account balance of payments gap of $6.9 billion in the January-to-March period, of which $3.1 billion came from the country's trade deficit, it said.
